description: Labelled claims for the Skeptic (does the source support the claim?). Source texts are the real OpenAlex abstracts of the demo project's papers (src/lib/demo-data.json). Written by Team 6 before any live run; expected verdicts follow the Skeptic's own definitions in src/server/ai/prompts.ts.

items.claim: Depressive symptoms and suicide rates among US adolescents increased between 2010 and 2015, especially among girls.
Social media use caused the increase in adolescent depression after 2010.
Economic factors such as unemployment were strongly linked to adolescent suicide rates.
This study proves that time on new media explains the rise in teen suicide.
Adolescents who play sports report lower rates of obesity.
In a cohort of 6,595 US adolescents, using social media for more than three hours a day was associated with internalizing problems.
Using social media for more than six hours a day triples the risk of internalizing problems in adolescents.
Social media use was consistently associated with externalizing problems in adolescents.
UK adolescents who use social media for more than three hours a day are at heightened risk of internalizing problems.
Social media use puts all young people at heightened risk of mental health problems.
In the UK Millennium Cohort Study, greater social media use was related to poor sleep and low self-esteem.
Social media use causes depression in UK teenagers through online harassment.
The association between social media use and depressive symptoms was larger for boys than for girls.
Among girls, five or more hours of daily social media use was linked to a 50% increase in depressive symptom scores compared with one to three hours.
A systematic review found that all domains of social media use correlated with depression, anxiety and psychological distress in adolescents.
The review established that social media use definitely harms adolescents' mental health.
Most of the studies in the review were randomised controlled trials.
In a large sample of English adolescents, the links between digital-screen time and mental well-being followed quadratic functions.
Moderate use of digital technology was found to be harmful to adolescents' well-being.
Digital technology use is beneficial for the mental health of all children.
